threads.thread_goal: Align on pilot scope, target audience, and success criteria.

messages.text:
Kicking off the Frontline Wellbeing and Communication Skills Program for our contact centre and reception colleagues under the project_title Frontline Wellbeing & Communication Skills Program.
I have started the needs analysis for T1 and will log findings in A1 so we can define the pilot scope in A2.
Initial thought is to focus on one contact centre team and one reception team, but I would like input on which groups make most sense and how many people we can realistically release without hurting service.
For success, I suggest we keep it simple: one metric on participation, one on perceived stress, and one on communication confidence.
@all, please share which teams you think should be in the first wave and any constraints I should factor into the interviews.

Thanks for starting this.
From the contact centre side, I suggest we use the inbound general enquiries team for the pilot. They see a wide range of calls, including some of the more emotional ones, so they will really test the communication and de-escalation content.
Headcount wise, that team has 18 people across shifts. I think we can realistically release 10–12 for the first round without dropping below minimum staffing, as long as we stagger sessions.
For reception, I would like to include the main building front desk, but I will need to confirm numbers.
On metrics, I like your three buckets. For communication confidence, we could use a short self-rating before and after the pilot.
I can support you with T2 once you have the first stressor themes from A1.

On my side, I can check with the complaints handling sub-team as an alternative or add-on.
They are smaller, 6 people, but they handle the toughest calls. If we include them, we need to be careful with coverage.
For success metrics, could we also track a simple indicator like number of escalations to a manager per shift for the pilot group, before and after? It will not be perfect, but it might show if the de-escalation skills are landing.
I will wait for your first summary in A1 before confirming which team is in scope for T2.

I can help draft the pilot scope in A2 once we agree on the teams.
Just to check I understood: we are thinking one inbound general enquiries team, maybe the complaints sub-team, and the main building reception.
For numbers, would it be ok if we start with around 20 people total so that scheduling is easier for T2, or is that too many for the first round?
On metrics, I can put together a simple one-page summary with the three indicators you mentioned so we can share it with supervisors.

Yes, that is roughly the idea.
Quick update on T1: I have already spoken with three frontline colleagues and one supervisor. Early themes going into A1 are high call volume, difficult callers, and limited time for proper breaks.
On numbers, 20 total feels on the high side for a first pilot given the shift constraints. Maybe we can aim for 14–16 instead: 10–12 from inbound general enquiries and 4 from reception.
For the complaints sub-team, I suggest we keep them for a second wave unless @45680 feels strongly otherwise.
If we agree on that, I will reflect it in A2 and T2 as the draft scope.

I am comfortable keeping the complaints sub-team for a later wave.
For this pilot, let us lock in:
- Inbound general enquiries: 12 people across shifts
- Main building reception: 4 people
That gives us 16 participants, which is manageable for scheduling and still gives us a good mix of phone and face-to-face interactions.
I can confirm the names with team leads as part of T2 once you have the draft list in A2.

Agree with that breakdown.
On success metrics, how about we formalise these three for the pilot:
1) Attendance rate for the sessions (participation)
2) Self-reported stress level at work, before and after
3) Self-reported confidence in handling difficult interactions, before and after
I like the idea of tracking escalations, but I worry it will be noisy in a short pilot window. We can still look at it informally.
If you are ok with these three, we can add them clearly into A2 so everyone sees what we are aiming for.

Those three metrics work for me and are realistic to collect within our 21-day window.
I will design a short pre and post survey for T1 and T9 that captures stress and confidence, and we will track attendance via A5 later.
I will also note in A2 that we may look at escalation numbers as a qualitative indicator, but not as a formal success metric.
Unless anyone objects today, I will treat these three as our primary measures for the pilot.

No objections from me.
I will update the draft in A2 to clearly list:
- 16 participants (12 contact centre, 4 reception)
- The three pilot metrics you described
- A short explanation of why we chose these groups
Once that is done, I will share the link here so supervisors can review before we finalise T2.

Sounds good.
To close the loop on metrics, I support the three you listed:
- Attendance rate
- Self-reported stress
- Self-reported confidence in difficult interactions
Let us confirm these as the official success criteria for the pilot so we can move ahead with T2 and the training design work.

Great, then we are aligned.
I will summarise in A1 and A2 that the pilot will cover 16 people (12 inbound general enquiries, 4 reception) and that our three primary metrics are attendance, stress, and confidence.
Next step from my side is to complete at least 10 frontline interviews for T1 and then share a short needs analysis summary in this channel.
From there, we can refine T2 and hand over to the training design threads.

threads.thread_goal: Design and finalise the training modules and wellbeing protocol.

messages.text:
Sharing a first draft of the training topics and micro-break ideas for feedback.
Based on the early themes in A1, I am proposing three communication modules for T3:
1) Foundations of calm, clear communication on the phone and at the desk
2) De-escalation techniques for upset or distressed callers and visitors
3) Setting boundaries and closing conversations respectfully when time is tight
For wellbeing, @89425 has started sketching a desk-based micro-break plan for T4 that would feed into A4.
Please review and suggest changes before we lock the final set of modules and the wellbeing protocol.

On the wellbeing side for T4, I have drafted a set of 8 low-impact desk exercises for A4:
- Neck and shoulder release
- Wrist and forearm stretch
- Seated spinal rotation
- Ankle circles
- Seated leg extensions
- Short breathing reset
- Eye focus change
- Micro walk in place (for those who can stand safely)
Each takes 30–60 seconds and can be done in normal work clothes. I will run them through a quick safety and accessibility check and then document them clearly in A4.
We should also agree how often we recommend these during a shift so it fits with service levels.

The three communication modules for T3 look on point.
For module 2 on de-escalation, can we make sure we include:
- How to recognise early signs that a caller is getting frustrated
- Simple phrases to acknowledge feelings without taking blame
- When and how to involve a supervisor
I can help draft a couple of role-play scenarios based on real calls so that A3 and T7 have concrete examples, not just theory.

I like the three-module structure.
One question: should we separate phone and reception examples, or keep them together? I am thinking of A3 and T7 and how clear the job aid and materials will be for each group.
Also, for module 3 on boundaries, could we add a small part on how to explain waiting times or delays in a way that feels respectful?

Good point.
My suggestion is:
- Keep the core techniques common for both phone and reception
- Use separate examples and role-plays for each group inside the same modules
That way A3 stays simple, but T7 can include different scenarios.
For boundaries, yes, we should include language for explaining queues, call-backs, and security procedures at reception.
I will update the T3 outline accordingly and share a short summary before we finalise.

On the micro-break protocol in A4, we need to make sure it aligns with HR policies and health and safety rules.
From a practical point of view, I would suggest we recommend:
- One 60–90 second micro-break roughly every hour for those on continuous calls
- Slightly longer movement during scheduled breaks, using a subset of your exercises
I will review your draft in A4 against A7 later in the compliance thread, but for now this frequency should be safe and realistic.
Please also note any contraindications in T4 so supervisors know when to adapt.

Understood.
I will adjust the draft in A4 to:
- Recommend 60–90 second micro-breaks about once per hour
- Suggest a short sequence for longer scheduled breaks
- Add clear notes on who should avoid certain movements and when to stop
I will also flag in T4 that final sign-off depends on HR and administration review, which we can handle in the compliance thread.
Once the text is ready, I will share a quick demo video internally if time allows, but the core protocol will be in A4.

I have now updated the T3 outline with:
- Early warning signs of escalation
- A simple three-step de-escalation approach (pause, acknowledge, offer next step)
- Clear guidance on when to involve a supervisor
For A3, I propose we structure the job aid around these three steps plus a small box with example phrases.
If there are no strong objections, I suggest we confirm these three modules as the final set for the pilot so that T7 can move ahead with materials.

No objections from me.
The three modules cover what our teams need most right now, and they are manageable within the time we have.
Let us confirm them as the final communication modules for the pilot so we can focus on building strong role-plays and job aids in T7.

Agreed.
I will reflect the three confirmed modules in A2 and make sure T7 materials match the structure you described.
For A3, I will start drafting the one-page job aid with the three-step de-escalation approach and example phrases, then share for review.

On the wellbeing protocol, I have reviewed your updated A4 draft.
The exercises are low impact, the frequency is reasonable, and the notes on when to adapt are clear.
From an HR perspective, I do not see any conflict with our current policies, as long as supervisors treat these as short pauses within existing break structures, not as extra breaks.
I suggest we approve this version of the desk-based wellbeing and micro-break protocol for the pilot, subject to the formal compliance check we will document in A7.

Thanks for the review.
Given your feedback and the safety checks already built into A4, I am comfortable approving this protocol for the pilot.
We will brief supervisors to integrate the micro-breaks into existing patterns so service levels are protected.
Let us mark this version of A4 as the agreed wellbeing and micro-break protocol for the pilot.

To summarise this thread:
- We have confirmed three communication modules for the pilot (foundations, de-escalation, boundaries)
- We have agreed on the desk-based wellbeing and micro-break protocol in A4
Next steps are to complete T3 and T4 and then move into T7 for materials.
I will capture this summary in A2 so that stakeholders have a single view of the pilot content.

threads.thread_goal: Lock training schedule and logistics with minimal service impact.

messages.text:
I have posted a draft training schedule for review in A5 for T6.
The proposal is:
- Two 90-minute sessions for communication modules
- One 60-minute session for wellbeing and micro-break practice
We would run each session three times to cover all 16 participants in small groups, without dropping below minimum staffing.
Please review the slots in A5 and flag any issues with shift patterns or reception coverage before we confirm the final schedule.

I have checked the draft in A5 against the inbound general enquiries rota.
Most slots look workable, but the Monday morning block would leave us one person short of our minimum threshold.
Could we move that group to mid-afternoon or to another day? If we shift by two hours, we should be fine.
For T6, we also need to make sure reception has cover during the wellbeing session, as they cannot close the desk.

I looked at the reception side.
For the main building desk, the current draft in A5 has both reception colleagues in the same session, which would leave the desk unmanned.
Maybe we can:
- Put one reception colleague in the first run of each module
- The other in the second run
That way there is always someone at the desk.
I can adjust the participant list in T2 once we agree on the pattern.

Thanks for spotting the staffing risks.
From an HR perspective, we must not go below the agreed minimum staffing levels, so we will need to adjust the schedule accordingly.
@4784, could you please:
- Move the Monday morning group to a mid-afternoon slot
- Stagger the reception colleagues as @605 suggested
Once you update A5, I will do a final check before we sign off T6.

I have updated A5:
- The Monday morning group is now scheduled for mid-afternoon on the same day
- Reception colleagues are split across different runs of each session so the desk is always covered
All groups still get the full set of modules and the wellbeing session.
Please re-check the new version and let me know if there are any remaining conflicts before we confirm T6.

I have re-checked the updated A5 against the latest rota.
With the new mid-afternoon slot, we stay at or above the minimum staffing level for all contact centre sessions.
The staggered reception pattern also works; there is always at least one person at the desk.
From an operations point of view, I am comfortable with this schedule for the pilot.

I have checked that the wellbeing session timing still allows enough time to demonstrate and practice the exercises from A4.
The 60-minute slot is sufficient for a short explanation, practice, and questions.
No issues from my side with the updated schedule in A5.
Once we confirm T6, I will align my availability for T8 to match these slots.

Given the latest checks:
- Contact centre staffing remains above minimum levels
- Reception coverage is maintained
- Trainers can attend the proposed slots
I suggest we approve the schedule in A5 as the final training plan for the pilot.
Once we confirm, we can use it for invitations (T5) and for attendance tracking during T8.

I support approving the current version of A5.
It balances training needs with service levels, and we have built in enough flexibility to handle minor changes.
Let us confirm this as the final training schedule for all pilot participants so we can move ahead with T5 and T8.

Now that we have a final schedule in A5, I will draft the participant communication for T5 with:
- Session dates and times
- Location or dial-in details
- Brief explanation of the program goals from A2
I will also include a short note on what to do if someone cannot attend their assigned slot, but we should agree the process for no-shows and rescheduling so that T8 can track it consistently.

On no-shows and rescheduling, I propose a simple process for T8:
- Trainers record attendance in A5 for each session
- Any no-shows are flagged in A5 on the same day
- Supervisors then move those names into the next available session slot, as long as staffing allows
If someone misses all three runs of a module, we log it and discuss with their supervisor after the pilot.
Does this work for HR and operations?

This approach is fine from HR side, as long as we keep the process transparent.
I suggest we add two clarifications:
- Supervisors should confirm that rescheduling does not push teams below minimum staffing
- If someone misses all runs, HR will join the follow-up conversation to understand the reasons
If we add these points to the instructions in A5 and T8, I am happy to confirm this as our process for handling no-shows and rescheduling.

Agreed.
With those clarifications, we have a clear and workable process:
- Trainers record attendance and flag no-shows in A5
- Supervisors reschedule into later runs, checking staffing
- HR joins if someone misses all runs
Let us confirm this as the process for no-shows and rescheduling during the pilot.

To close this thread:
- We have approved the final training schedule in A5
- We have agreed on the process for handling no-shows and rescheduling
I will summarise this in A2 and make sure T5 invitations and T8 attendance tracking reflect the agreed process.

threads.thread_goal: Ensure compliance and define governance for ongoing rollout.

messages.text:
I am sharing initial policy review notes and a draft governance proposal for the program.
For T11, I have started using A7 to check the modules and wellbeing protocol against:
- Working time and breaks
- Equality and inclusion
- Health and safety
So far, the content in A3 and A4 looks compatible with our policies, but I will complete the checklist before we sign off.
For governance (T10), I have a first outline in A8 that suggests HR owns content, supervisors own scheduling, and administration supports documentation.
Please review and comment before we confirm compliance and long-term ownership.

On the wellbeing side, I can confirm that the exercises in A4 are low impact and can be adapted for different physical conditions.
I have added notes in A4 about:
- Optional standing variations
- When to avoid certain movements
- Encouraging staff to stop if they feel discomfort
This should support the health and safety part of A7.
If you see any gaps from a policy angle, let me know and I will adjust T4 accordingly.

From the contact centre side, I have checked that the micro-break recommendations in A4 can fit within existing break structures.
Supervisors will need clear guidance that these are short pauses within the shift, not extra formal breaks, which you have already noted in A7.
On governance in A8, I suggest we add that supervisors are responsible for running the short wellbeing check-ins from T12, using a simple script agreed with HR.

I have read through the draft in A8.
To make roles clearer, could we spell out:
- Who updates A2 and A3 when we change content
- Who maintains A5 for future waves
I can help document this in T10 once we agree.
Also, for T12, I can support drafting a short check-in script that supervisors can use at the start of a shift.

Good suggestions.
I have updated A8 to propose:
- HR maintains A2, A3, and A4 (content and policy alignment)
- Contact centre and reception supervisors maintain A5 for their teams (scheduling and attendance)
- Administration supports version control and storage for all artifacts
For T12, I would welcome your help drafting a short, inclusive check-in script that does not ask for sensitive health information but still surfaces stress levels.

I will draft a simple T12 script along these lines:
- One quick question on how people are feeling about the day ahead
- One question on any specific stressors they want to flag
- A reminder of the micro-break options from A4
I will keep it short so it fits into a 3–5 minute huddle.
Once drafted, I will add it to A8 as an appendix for supervisors.

I have now completed the A7 checklist for T11:
- Working time and breaks: compliant, as micro-breaks sit within existing structures
- Equality and inclusion: content is neutral and accessible, with adaptations noted
- Health and safety: exercises are low impact, with clear stop guidance
I do not see any conflicts with labour legislation or internal HR policies.
From my side, I am ready to sign off that the program, as described in A2, A3, and A4, complies with our requirements.

Thanks for completing the checklist.
Given your review and the adjustments we made in A4, I am comfortable confirming that the program is safe to run from an operational point of view.
We will brief supervisors on how to apply the guidance in A7 and A8 so they stay within policy.
I suggest we formally sign off that the program complies with labour and internal policies, based on your T11 work.

I agree with signing off compliance.
On governance in A8, the split you proposed makes sense in practice:
- HR for content and policy
- Supervisors for scheduling and check-ins
- Administration for documentation
We should also note how often we will review the program after the pilot. Maybe a quarterly review with HR and supervisors to start?

Quarterly review sounds reasonable for the first year.
I have updated A8 and T10 to state:
- HR convenes a quarterly review with supervisors to look at feedback (A6) and adjust content
- Administration keeps A2, A3, A4, A5, A7, and A8 up to date in the shared drive
- Supervisors run T12 check-ins and feed insights back to HR
If everyone is comfortable with this, we can confirm this governance model and review cadence for the ongoing program.

I am comfortable with that structure.
It is clear who does what, and the quarterly review gives us a regular moment to adjust based on frontline feedback.
Let us confirm this governance and review cadence as the long-term ownership model for the program.

To summarise this thread:
- A7 checklist is complete and shows no conflicts with labour or internal policies
- We have signed off that the program content in A2, A3, and A4 is compliant
- A8 now defines clear governance, with HR, supervisors, and administration each owning specific parts, plus a quarterly review cadence
I will store the final versions of A7 and A8 and reference them in the pilot communications so stakeholders know how the program is governed.

threads.thread_goal: Review pilot feedback and decide on adjustments before scaling.

messages.text:
I have posted a draft feedback and impact evaluation report in A6 for T9.
Headline results from the pilot:
- Attendance: 15 out of 16 participants completed all three sessions
- Self-reported stress: average score dropped from 7.1 to 5.9 (on a 0–10 scale)
- Confidence in handling difficult interactions: average score increased from 5.8 to 7.3
Qualitative comments highlight that the de-escalation phrases and the breathing reset from A4 were especially useful.
Please review A6 and share what you think we should keep, change, or drop before we plan the next wave.

Looking at A6, the numbers are encouraging.
From the debriefs, I heard that:
- The role-plays in module 2 felt very realistic
- Module 3 on boundaries was helpful but a bit rushed
- Some staff would like more practice on handling repeat callers
For the next wave, I would keep all three modules but consider:
- Adding a bit more time or a follow-up micro-session for boundaries
- Including one extra scenario on repeat callers in A3 and T7.

On the wellbeing side, feedback in A6 shows that:
- The breathing reset and neck/shoulder release were used most often
- The micro walk in place was harder to fit in during busy periods
- Some people forgot the exercises after a few days
For the next wave, I suggest we:
- Keep all exercises in A4 but highlight a core set of 3–4 for daily use
- Add a small visual reminder in A3 or a separate card so people remember the steps
- Work with supervisors via T12 to weave one exercise into team huddles.

I noticed in A6 that a few participants found the first module a bit long on theory.
Maybe for the next wave we can:
- Shorten the introductory slides in T7
- Move faster into examples and practice
Also, one person mentioned that the invitations did not clearly explain the time commitment. I can adjust T5 templates so expectations are clearer.

From the supervisor side, I agree with your observations.
I would keep:
- All three communication modules
- The breathing reset and key stretches from A4
I would change:
- Pace of module 1 (less theory)
- More time for boundaries practice
I would drop:
- Nothing major, but we can trim some overlapping content between modules 1 and 2.
If we align on this, we can update A3 and T7 before the next cohort.

This matches what I see in the survey comments.
To make it concrete, for the next wave I propose we:
Keep:
- All three modules
- Core wellbeing exercises (breathing, neck/shoulder, wrist/forearm)
Change:
- Shorten theory in module 1
- Add one repeat-caller scenario
- Emphasise a core set of 3–4 exercises in A4
Drop:
- Some overlapping explanation between modules 1 and 2
Does anyone see anything else we should remove or add before we lock this adjustment list?

I would add one more change: make the examples slightly more tailored for reception.
Some reception staff said in A6 that a few scenarios felt very call-centre focused.
We can adjust A3 and T7 to include at least one reception-specific scenario in each module.
Apart from that, I agree with your keep/change/drop list.

On wellbeing, I support your list.
I will:
- Highlight the core 3–4 exercises in A4
- Prepare a very simple visual reminder that can sit next to A3
- Coordinate with supervisors via T12 so they can pick one exercise for team huddles
No need to drop any exercises; we will just be clearer about which ones are everyday essentials.

I can help update T7 materials to:
- Reduce theory slides in module 1
- Add the repeat-caller and reception-specific scenarios
- Make the time commitment clearer in T5 invitations
Once we agree the final keep/change/drop list, I will reflect it in A2 so stakeholders see how we are evolving the program.

Let me summarise the adjustments we seem to agree on for the next wave:
Keep:
- All three communication modules
- Full set of wellbeing exercises, with a highlighted core set
Change:
- Shorter theory in module 1
- More time and practice for boundaries
- Add repeat-caller and reception-specific scenarios
- Stronger visual reminders for wellbeing
- Clearer time commitment in invitations
Drop:
- Some overlapping explanation between modules 1 and 2
If there are no objections, we can confirm this as our decision on what to keep, change, and drop before scaling.

No objections from me.
This list reflects both the data in A6 and what we heard in the room.
Let us confirm these as the elements we will keep, change, and drop for the next wave, and then update A2, A3, A4, and T7 accordingly.

Great, then we are aligned.
I will finalise A6 with a short section summarising the keep/change/drop decisions and update A2 to describe the next-wave design.
Thanks everyone for the input; this gives us a clear path to scale the program while staying close to what frontline staff actually found useful.
